Despite Mac shipments falling 11% in Q3 2026, Apple's market share rose from 8.5% to 9.5% as the overall market saw shipments plunge 20.1%, according to a new report from IDC. Here are the details.

Apple Outperforms Most of the PC Market in Challenging Environment

IDC today published its report on worldwide PC shipments for the third quarter of 2026, noting that while Apple's Mac shipments have declined year-over-year, it has clearly outperformed the broader market.

According to IDC's preliminary data, Apple shipped 5.9 million Macs during the third quarter of 2026, down 11.3% from 6.7 million in the year-ago quarter.

However, the overall PC market declined even more significantly, with worldwide shipments falling 20.1% year-over-year to 62.7 million units.

As a result, Apple's share of global PC shipments actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5%.

This result keeps Apple in fourth place, behind Lenovo, which led the rankings with 14.9 million shipments and a 23.8% market share, followed by HP with 10.3 million shipments and a 16.5% share, and Dell with 7.6 million shipments and a 12.1% share.

Among the top five PC brands, HP saw the steepest year-over-year decline at 30.9%. ASUS, meanwhile, posted the smallest decline, falling 8.6% year-over-year with shipments of 5.5 million units for an 8.7% market share.

Here's what IDC said:

Looking ahead, IDC said that "channel concerns about weak demand amid high inventory and high prices could fuel promotional activity in the near term," while adding that "prices will remain well above year-ago levels."

The firm also noted that the economy has weakened since the prior quarter, which may further erode demand and make "the outlook for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027 even gloomier."
